qt: to the Commission Jeannette Baljeu (Renew) Subject:

A seagoing vessel is permitted to operate on renewable methanol, and its use counts in full towards FuelEU Maritime compliance. However, an inland waterway operator cannot yet purchase a standard, type-approved methanol engine. This is because methanol is not included as a fuel under the European rules governing engines (the NRMM Regulation). A recent study by the European Parliament’s Committee on Transport and Tourism describes this as a barrier to investment. The Commission is currently amending those rules, but only for hydrogen, owing to concerns about formaldehyde emissions from methanol. As a result, businesses wishing to invest now may have to wait for years. 1.
Is the Commission prepared to include methanol in this amendment already and to lay down any requirements regarding formaldehyde at a later stage?
How does the Commission intend to ensure that inland waterway operators can purchase a type-approved methanol engine as soon as possible?
Why does technology neutrality apply to methanol at sea but not on inland waterways?
